newsitem.title: USA: O'Sullivan sees Q1 earnings off up to 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: O'Sullivan sees Q1 earnings off up to 50 pct.

text.p: O'Sullivan Corp said Thursday it expects to report lower sales and earnings in the first quarter than in the year-earlier period, primarily as a result of lower sales and higher raw material costs.
The company said it expected sales to fall between eight percent and nine percent, while earnings would be off 40 percent to 50 percent.
In the first quarter of 1996 the company had sales of $56.2 million and earned $0.26 a share.
Sales in the first quarter of 1997, said the company, are behind last year's in both its plastics business and its Melnor subsidiary.

The company did, however, forecast a stronger second quarter based on customers' forecasted requirements and aggressive cost reductions. It also said that a turnaround at Melnor should result in significant gains even if sales remained below expectations.
O'Sullivan makes premium vinyl coverstock for auto, medical and office supply products. Melnor makes lawn and garden watering products.
